name: Howden Joinery
headline: A UK kitchen supplier to builders whose margins far exceed every rival's.
what_short: Kitchens and joinery sold to UK builders
what_it_does: Howden Joinery sells kitchens and joinery to small builders through 975 depots (893 in the UK), always in stock, with confidential local pricing and trade credit. About 38% of the cost of goods is made in its own factories. In June 2026 it also bought DIY Kitchens, an online seller to ordinary consumers.
why_it_passed: Its operating margin was 14.7% in 2025, against -2.1% at Travis Perkins and 4.3% at Wickes, and it held between 12.6% and 19.2% for the decade.
Gross margin stayed between 60.8% and 62.8% as it raised prices at the start of 2022, 2023 and 2026.
Before tax it earned about 64% on the capital the business needed in 2019, with almost no goodwill, and had no borrowing for eleven years until 2026.
The analysis found management honest and able.
why_not_now: At 788p a share the price sits at the bottom of the analysis's value range of 780p to 1,044p, but no case in that range earns the roughly 10% a year the analysis requires. The analysis's fair price is 499p, and even the top of the range valued at that standard is only 567p.
watch: Margins have narrowed: operating margin averaged 16.6% in 2015 to 2019 against 14.7% in 2023 to 2025, and the cash the business produces fell from about 10% of sales to 5% to 6%.
In June 2026 it took on its first borrowing in eleven years, a 240 million pound term loan for the DIY Kitchens deal.
The buyback has no stated price limit, and has run above the bottom of the value range.
